item.title: California Senator Scott Wiener Wins Congress Seat, Eyes Federal AI Regulation
item.description:
California Senator Scott Wiener Wins Congress Seat, Eyes Federal AI Regulation

California state senator Scott Wiener has won the open U.S. House seat in San Francisco, positioning him to influence federal AI policy.

🗳️ Election Victory

  • Won a tight congressional race for former Speaker of the House Nancy Pelosi’s open San Francisco seat.
  • Declared the victor and was interviewed only a few hours later.

🔍 AI Policy Background

  • AI regulation is a cornerstone of his political career.
  • Has been increasingly focused on AI in recent years, adopting concerns of the AI safety movement.

📜 Legislative Record

  • SB 1047 (2024) – Authored by Wiener; set to become the first real piece of frontier AI legislation before it was vetoed by California Governor Gavin Newsom.
  • SB 53 – A lighter‑touch bill sponsored by Wiener that Governor Newsom signed.
  • Both bills have inspired proposed federal legislation.
Bill Status Federal Influence
SB 1047 Vetoed after being poised as first frontier AI law Inspired proposed federal legislation
SB 53 Signed into law (lighter‑touch) Inspired proposed federal legislation

🚀 Congressional Priorities

  • Cited a METR report suggesting Anthropic achieved recursive self‑improvement as “very concerning” and said we are “quickly running out of time to regulate AI.”
  • Hoped Congress would take decisive action before the end of the year, but noted that “does not appear to be happening.”
  • Calls for “a strong, empowered, nimble federal regulator,” referencing Representative Ro Khanna’s proposal.
  • Emphasizes whistleblower protections, testing and auditing requirements, and a kill‑switch requirement.
  • Would be eager to serve on a congressional select committee on artificial intelligence if formed.
  • Says “States are, as Brandeis says, laboratories” and should remain nimble while Congress acts “in a way that is truly meaningful and that meets the moment.”

🤝 Funding and Industry Relations

  • Received over $3 million from Public First Action, a nonprofit that supports AI regulation and receives substantial funding from Anthropic.
  • Defended the contribution, writing that he was “the first lawmaker in the country to introduce AI regulation and the first to pass it and get it implemented.”
  • Opponents criticized him for being “too close to the AI industry,” which he called “shockingly cynical” and a false claim.

📈 Future Impact

  • Warns that “We’re in a moment that is very dangerous in terms of the risk of loss of control over AI.”
  • Stresses the need to “slow this down” because AI is “moving very quickly, and we could sleepwalk into a disaster.”
  • Says dealing with “recursive self‑improvement” is “potentially a recipe for total loss of control.”

#AIRegulation #Congress #ScottWiener #AIrisk

Source: Nancy Pelosi’s replacement is ready to regulate AI

item.title: President announces plans to form an AI force and appoint AI czar
item.description:
President announces plans to form an AI force and appoint AI czar

President Trump has announced his intention to establish an “AI force” led by an “AI czar.” This initiative comes amid increasing calls from the industry and political spectrum to slow down AI development.

⚙️ Key details

  • The administration aims to foster the growth of the AI industry without hindering it.
  • The President compared the proposed AI force to the creation of the Space Force.
  • No specific timeline or leadership candidates have been announced for the position.
  • The President stated that “Only High I.Q. individuals need apply” for the czar role.

💡 Why it matters

  • Data centers: The President asserted that data centers are “wealthy and prestigious” and claimed they raise salaries, lower taxes, and improve community safety, though no evidence was provided to support these claims.

#AI #Government #Policy #Technology

Source: Trump now says he wants to form an ‘AI Force’

item.title: U.S. Census Bureau Proposes AI Updates to Business Trends and Outlook Survey
item.description:
U.S. Census Bureau Proposes AI Updates to Business Trends and Outlook Survey

The U.S. Census Bureau is seeking comment by October 9, 2026, on revisions to the Business Trends and Outlook Survey (BTOS), which include updates to how the agency collects data on artificial intelligence.

🔍 Overview

BTOS is the only biweekly business tendency survey produced by the federal statistical system. It uses ongoing data collection to provide granular, timely, and high-frequency information regarding current trends and economic conditions. The survey targets all nonfarm employer businesses in the United States, Puerto Rico, and the District of Columbia with receipts of $1,000 or more.

⚙️ Key details

The Bureau is requesting approval for several changes to the survey structure:

  • AI Supplement: The Bureau seeks to repeat the AI supplement with minor content changes that have undergone cognitive testing.
  • Core Question Additions: The Bureau is requesting to add three core questions regarding AI and one new core question regarding business uncertainty (which has also been cognitively tested).
  • Data Frequency: The Bureau is exploring methods to publish and collect data from the AI supplement more frequently than annually, but less frequently than bi-weekly.

🧩 How it works

To reduce respondent burden, the Bureau will implement skip logic, ensuring AI-related questions are only asked of businesses that report using AI.

Question Focus Source/Status
Generative AI usage Moved from AI supplement to core questions
Impact of AI on total number of employees Moved from AI supplement to core questions
Impact of AI on new employees New question (cognitively tested)
Business uncertainty New core question (cognitively tested)

#USCensusBureau #BTOS #EconomicData #GenerativeAI

Source: FRN on Revising the Business Trends and Outlook Survey - The Census Project
